Everything else in the contract is covered and passing; nothing already written changes." No new repository file: the harness criterion 16 needs is written into the test's own temp dir at run time, which is what "Add test fixtures" allows. I copied all fifteen byte-for-byte out of `.dev/inprocess/114-kit-page-narration/tdd/result.json`. READ THEM AS THE RECORD OF THE EARLIER ROUND, NOT OF THE TREE TODAY: IMPLEMENT has since run (commit cfbbbf5), so row 1's counts ("878 tests … 862 pass, 16 fail") and row 13's two failures are no longer what the commands print. I am reporting that rather than quietly restating stale numbers. WHY THE WHOLE-SUITE RUN IS THE PROOF. The fix direction: "`bun test` from the repository root is the proof, and `0 fail` is the signal: a single-file run always exits 1 here because `bunfig.toml` turns coverage on with a floor one file cannot reach." Confirmed: `bun test ts/metalang/render.test.ts` alone reports 73.42% of lines against the 0.75 floor. The whole suite still reports 95.60% of functions and 96.54% of lines, so criterion 11 is unmoved by this round. CRITERION 16 — WHAT THE TEST DOES, AND WHY IT IS SHAPED THIS WAY. The criterion is about what a page SHOWS, and the line is drawn in the browser — it is in no page's own text. So the test writes the real page with the real renderer (`renderWith(LANGUAGE_FILE, …)`), then runs the page's real bundle entry (`PAGE_SOURCE`, which is `client.tsx`, the file the contract's Surfaces names as "where the helper's announcement is read") over that page in a real DOM, and counts the innermost elements whose text says it cannot be narrated. One child process per case, because a bundle mounts a page once. No seam was invented and no signature touched: the test drives the page end to end, through types that already exist. ONE SIDE OF CRITERION 16 PASSES TODAY, AND I AM SAYING SO RATHER THAN DRESSING IT UP. The criterion has two sides and both are tested, as rails-test-code Practice 4 requires. The silent side fails now (expected 1 line, received 0) and is the forcing function. The announced side passes now vacuously — nothing draws any line yet, so "shows none" is trivially true. The criterion's row is `red: true` because the criterion fails today; I did not split the announced side into a `red: false` row, because its behaviour is behaviour this change builds, which decision `green-criterion` forbids recording as passing. The announced side is not idle after IMPLEMENT: it is what catches a page that says it cannot be narrated when the helper did announce itself, which is the defect `What to do` item 9 exists to prevent. ONE THING THE TEST CANNOT PROVE, REPORTED AS A GAP RATHER THAN LEFT QUIET. `What to do` item 9 requires the reading to happen "once the deferred scripts have run rather than at mount". No test here proves that ordering, because this machine cannot execute a page's scripts inside a document that is still parsing. Both routes are blocked and I verified each: under bun, jsdom 31's `runScripts: 'dangerously'` dies in `node_modules/jsdom/lib/jsdom/browser/Window.js:60` with `TypeError: The "context" argument must be of type object. Received type symbol (Symbol(vm_context_no_contextify))`; under this machine's node (v23.5.0) jsdom 31 cannot even be imported — `node_modules/undici/lib/interceptor/decompress.js:78 TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'bind')`, because `zlib.createZstdDecompress` does not exist in that node. So the harness parses the page first and runs the bundle after, and it both sets the announcement before running the bundle and dispatches `DOMContentLoaded` and `load` afterwards, so an implementation that checks `document.readyState` and one that waits for an event are both read correctly. A mount-time reading would still pass here. The implementer and the reviewers should treat the deferred ordering as covered by the contract's own words and by the page's inline/deferred layout, not by a test. BOTH NEW TESTS WERE PROVEN SATISFIABLE, THEN THE PROOF WAS THROWN AWAY. A test nobody can turn green is not a forcing function, it is a wall, so I checked: a four-line throwaway addition to client.tsx (read `window.__jarvisStory`, append one `

The kit readme is a template literal inside `readmeText()`, so a backtick in the new sentence must be written `\``. My first throwaway sentence used bare backticks and broke kit.ts outright — 20 tests failed. It is a spike artifact, not a test requirement, but it is the obvious way to get it wrong. KINDS. It is prose, so a prose test is the only kind there is; the test name says exactly what has to be written so nobody has to guess. DRY. The script's path is written out again in kit.test.ts rather than imported from the renderer, as a named constant with the reason beside it — the same reason the file already records for its own story-helper test: "The tag itself is written out rather than read from the renderer, so this says what a released kit has to carry rather than agreeing with whatever the renderer happens to write." The two criterion-16 cases share one `shownBy` helper and one harness; nothing is written twice. NO COMMIT, NO PUSH. Nothing was staged or committed. findings.summary: Rails 6/7 (every assertion can fail; derived from the criterion): contract What-to-do item 9 requires the helper announcement to be read once the deferred scripts have run, not at mount, but no test can fail for a mount-time reading, so that required behavior is unpinned. The test author's own notes concede this.
findings.evidence: ts/metalang/render.test.ts HARNESS (about lines 365-395): the announced case sets dom.window.__jarvisStory = true and globalThis.__jarvisStory = true BEFORE `await import(entry)`. A bundle that reads the flag at mount therefore sees it and passes the announced case, and the silent case is identical either way. The contract (item 9) says 'the page's bundle is written inline and runs before any deferred script, so the reading happens once the deferred scripts have run rather than at mount'. The notes' claim that this cannot be modelled on this machine is not true for ordering: the harness can import the bundle first, wait for the root to draw, then set the announcement, then dispatch DOMContentLoaded and load. That is the real browser order (inline bundle, then the deferred helper announces). With that order a mount-time reader draws the line in the announced case and the test fails. No jsdom runScripts is needed.
findings.fix: In the HARNESS, for the announced case, set __jarvisStory only after the bundle has mounted and the root has children, and before dispatching DOMContentLoaded and load. Keep the silent case as is. Add a case or comment confirming that a page whose helper announces itself after mount shows no line, so the announced-case test fails for a mount-time implementation. Re-prove it satisfiable with a throwaway load-time implementation and re-run bun test from the root.

findings.summary: Seven coverage rows assert the criterion is still RED when it passes in the tree this result is submitted against, and row 13 states exit codes the result's own redProof contradicts; the only authorization cited for keeping them is the orchestrator's fix-direction file, not Tim's approved `green-criterion` wording.
findings.evidence: Decision `green-criterion` (contract.md:17) is the approved wording that governs a row: "A criterion that only guards behavior this contract requires to keep working is recorded in the coverage list as `red: false` carrying the reason in `whyPassing`; every other criterion is still RED, a `red: false` row with no reason is refused, and a `red: true` row that carries one is refused." Rows for acceptance items 2, 3, 4, 5, 9, 12 and 13 are recorded `red: true`, which asserts the criterion fails. All seven pass today: `cd /Users/timothystockstill/code/macos/4thWAIV/agent-guard/.claude/worktrees/kit-walkthrough-targets && bun test` → 879 pass, 2 fail, and the only two failures are the new criterion-16 and criterion-17 tests; `bun test ts/metalang/app.test.tsx` → 207 pass, 0 fail (items 2-5); `bun test ts/metalang/kit.test.ts` → "refuses a kit asset with style.css taken out of it" (pass), "refuses a kit asset with syntax.css taken out of it" (pass), "the page it draws loads the story helper, so a released kit can be narrated" (pass) (items 9, 12). Row 13 goes further and records as its evidence "`bun run typecheck` — exit 2, TS7016 on the jsdom import at ts/metalang/app.test.tsx(12,23)" and "`bun run lint` — exit 1, @typescript-eslint/no-unsafe-call at ts/metalang/app.test.tsx:1784:18"; I ran both from the worktree root: `bun run typecheck` → exit 0, `bun run lint` → exit 0, and the result's own redProof pastes those same two commands at exit 0. The record therefore contradicts the proof attached to it. Those criteria are green because IMPLEMENT landed them in commit cfbbbf5 "Implement the kit page narration targets" (ts/metalang/app.tsx, render.ts, arch.yaml, metalang.yaml, ci.yml, package.json, bun.lock, app.test.tsx). The authorization the notes give is "THE FIFTEEN ROWS ARE THE PRIOR ROUND'S, VERBATIM, BECAUSE THE FIX DIRECTION SAYS SO", quoting `.dev/inprocess/114-kit-page-narration/fixes-for-the-page-saying-so.md`; the quotes are accurate (that file's last line reads "Every other criterion must stay as it is — fifteen rows unchanged, eight of them red for the reasons already recorded and seven carrying the reason they pass"), but that file is a stage direction, not Tim, and it contradicts itself — its opening line reads "Everything else in the contract is covered and passing" while its closing line orders eight rows to stay red. rails-decisions: "Anchor approval to Tim's actual words, never to 'it's already in the code'" and "No one is exempt — audit the orchestrator's steps too, not just the worker's." The notes disclose the staleness in prose ("Today `bun test` is 881 tests, 879 pass, 2 fail"), so nothing is hidden, but the machine-read coverage record the gate accepts still asserts seven failures that do not exist and two exit codes that are wrong, and it asks the reader to interpret it against a tree that no longer exists: "READ THEM AS THE RECORD OF THE EARLIER ROUND, NOT OF THE TREE TODAY".

findings.summary: Four `red: false` rows carry a `whyPassing` reason that is untrue of the tree, each one asserting the implementing code has not been written when commit cfbbbf5 wrote it.
findings.evidence: The requirement is decision `green-criterion` (contract.md:17), which permits `red: false` only "carrying the reason in `whyPassing`" — the reason the criterion passes today. Four of the seven `red: false` rows state facts that are false now. Row 6 (`data-part`/`data-col` targets): "nothing has yet touched the renderer, so every one of those targets is still spelled and drawn as it is today" and "The criterion is the guard that the two new identity attributes do not move or rename them when IMPLEMENT adds them" — IMPLEMENT has run: commit cfbbbf5 changed ts/metalang/app.tsx (109 lines) and ts/metalang/render.ts (22 lines). Row 7 (identical bytes twice): "The criterion guards that the member and declaration identities, and the story helper tag, do not put anything render-dependent into the page; it cannot fail before that code exists" — that code exists: `grep -n 'data-declaration\|data-member' ts/metalang/app.tsx` → `780: data-member={identityOf(member)}` and `1508: data-declaration={declaredId ?? undefined}`, and `ts/metalang/render.ts:68` holds `const STORY_HELPER = '<script defer src="/api/packages/story.js"></script>'`. Row 8 (the three rules' fixtures): "What is RED in guardrails.test.ts is a different test — `the drawing path > writes no word of the language out`, the fifteen literals rule 1 flags in app.tsx — which is the rule's recorded impact on existing code for IMPLEMENT to clear" — nothing in that file is RED: `bun test ts/metalang/guardrails.test.ts` → 17 pass, 0 fail, including `(pass) the drawing path > writes no word of the language out`. Row 11 (coverage floor): "the exit 1 is the sixteen failing tests rather than the coverage gate" and "which cannot fail before that code exists" — exit 1 is two failing tests, per the result's own redProof ("879 pass / 2 fail") and my own run, and the code exists per the greps above. Each row's stated ground for passing is therefore not the ground on which it passes, which is the condition the test stage is judged against: a `red: false` row whose reason is untrue is a FAIL. As in the finding above, the only authorization offered is the orchestrator's `fixes-for-the-page-saying-so.md` ordering the rows kept verbatim, which cannot make a false statement of the tree true and is not Tim's approval of this record.

observations.summary: The criterion-17 test requires the readme paragraph to contain the literal `/api/packages/story.js`, which criterion 17's own words do not require.
observations.evidence: ts/metalang/kit.test.ts:106-112 finds the paragraph by `/narrat/i.test(paragraph) && paragraph.includes(NARRATION_SCRIPT)` with `NARRATION_SCRIPT = '/api/packages/story.js'`, then asserts `expect(narration).toBeDefined()`, so the readme must name the path. Acceptance 17 says only "The kit readme says a drawn page reaches out to its origin for the narration script", and decision `helper-absent` (contract.md:25) says "The kit readme gains a sentence saying a drawn page reaches out to its origin for that script." The test also forces the sentence into its own `\n\n`-delimited paragraph.
observations.nonBlockingReason: No new decision-level element is introduced: the path is already approved in `What to do` item 4 and named in Acceptance 12 and at ts/metalang/render.ts:68, so "that script" naming it is a defensible reading rather than a requirement change, and paragraph structure is test-internal with no blast radius.

observations.summary: The ordering `What to do` item 9 requires — the reading taken once the deferred scripts have run rather than at mount — is proven by no test, and the notes ask the implementer and the reviewers to treat it as covered by the contract's words.
observations.evidence: Contract `What to do` item 9: "the page's bundle is written inline and runs before any deferred script, so the reading happens once the deferred scripts have run rather than at mount." The harness at ts/metalang/render.test.ts:350-392 parses the page first, then imports the entry, sets the announcement before that import, and dispatches `DOMContentLoaded` and `load` afterwards; the notes state plainly "A mount-time reading would still pass here" and give the verified failure for both routes (jsdom 31 under bun dies at node_modules/jsdom/lib/jsdom/browser/Window.js:60; under node v23.5.0 it cannot be imported). The notes then say "The implementer and the reviewers should treat the deferred ordering as covered by the contract's own words and by the page's inline/deferred layout, not by a test."
observations.nonBlockingReason: No Acceptance criterion states the ordering — Acceptance 16 asks only what the page shows in each of the two cases, and both cases are tested — and the gap was disclosed with reproducible evidence rather than reported as checked, so nothing is laundered; whether the test is thereby weakened is the TDD lens's ruling, not a decision or approval defect.

observations.summary: The criterion-16 page is drawn with an empty bundle and the entry is imported as a module instead, so the shipped page shape (inline bundle inside the real shell) is never exercised.
observations.evidence: ts/metalang/render.test.ts:410 renders the page as `await renderWith(LANGUAGE_FILE, page, () => Promise.resolve(''))`, and the harness is spawned over `join(dirname(LANGUAGE_FILE), PAGE_SOURCE)` (ts/metalang/render.test.ts:424), i.e. ts/metalang/client.tsx imported directly, with jsdom constructed without `runScripts`.
observations.nonBlockingReason: No interface or seam is assumed that the contract does not already state: `PAGE_SOURCE` is an existing export at ts/metalang/render.ts:33, `renderWith` is used with its existing signature, and Surfaces (contract.md:67) names ts/metalang/client.tsx as "where the helper's announcement is read"; the fidelity question belongs to the TDD lens.
